title: CRAGMOOR OUTFITTERS catalog rescue: neutralize an 8-SKU mixed-light optics batch to an in-frame grey card, knock each onto one matched pure-white marketplace hero, prep the two supplied distributor-mark scans for print, then data-merge one press-ready product line-sheet card per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork catalog-cleanup brief for a hands-off drop-ship store that sells outdoor optics and field gear through an online storefront (the real listing asked to 'audit and clean up product catalog — titles, descriptions, tags, and images'; the data-feed/inventory-sync/MAP/404 work is operations, not Adobe, and is excluded). Laundered to a fictional store, 'Cragmoor Outfitters Co.', and two fictional distributors, 'Harlow Optics Group' and 'Vantage Field Supply' — no real company, product line, person, or trademark is named anywhere; SKU names and model codes are invented. Generic online-store and third-party marketplace channels are referenced only as the delivery-channel spec (the pure-white hero requirement), never by any real platform or brand name in the scene. REPOSITIONED for connector reality and to clear the hardness bar: the killed original was one SKU run through ten mostly-parameterless auto-ops and squared the hero with image_fill_area (which cannot extend a canvas). The corrected design scales to the real workload the brief points at — eight heterogeneous drop-ship SKUs that arrive shot by different distributors under mismatched light, each with a photographic 18% grey card and a small white swatch laid in frame as an honest neutral reference — and makes the Adobe chain do the work the brief rewards: neutralize every SKU to its own in-frame grey card so the whole catalog page shares one white point and one brightness, isolate each product onto a pure #FFFFFF marketplace hero at an exact square pixel size (downscaled from camera-scale distributor JPEGs, never enlarged), triage the two distributor brand marks — both supplied as the same kind of raw raster scan, with the SKU sheet referencing only neutral produced-mark names so no client-supplied field reveals which treatment each mark needs — and prep each correctly for print, and finally run a genuinely hand-authored InDesign product-card template through a one-file-per-row data-merge to emit a press-ready line-sheet card per SKU. Neutrality is graded on a retained card-bearing master per SKU (the delivered hero crops the card out), so the grader always has the reference region it needs.
one_line_ask: Take eight inconsistent distributor-supplied optics/field-gear product photos (each carrying an 18% grey card and white swatch in frame, shot under different casts and exposures), neutralize each one to its grey card so the whole catalog reads as one matched white point, isolate every product onto a pure #FFFFFF square marketplace hero at an exact pixel size without ever enlarging the source, prep the two distributor brand marks (both supplied as raw scans) so each drops cleanly into the card's mark window and stays sharp at print size, then data-merge the client's authored InDesign product-card template against the SKU sheet to produce one press-ready line-sheet card per SKU.
full_brief:
I run a hands-off online store, Cragmoor Outfitters, selling outdoor optics and field gear — thermal monoculars, laser rangefinders, spotting scopes, trail cameras, tripod heads and the like. My two distributors dump product photos that are all over the place: shot on off-white or grey seamless by different people on different days, some under cool LED shop light, some under warm tungsten, one under greenish work-lights, a few over- or under-exposed. Side by side on a collection page they look like eight different stores, and several get rejected by the marketplace channels that demand a pure-white background. As part of the catalog cleanup I need a repeatable Adobe pipeline, proven end-to-end on my current eight-SKU batch, that turns this mess into clean, matched, marketplace-ready listing assets.

Here is what I need back. First, the photos: to make 'matched' honest I had the distributors drop a standard 18% grey card and a small white swatch into the corner of every frame. Bring all eight to one consistent look by neutralizing each shot to the grey card it carries — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your corrected frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set sits on one white point and one brightness. We need the eight optics to look true to their real finishes and to read as one consistent set on our store — a matched, professional product line. Keep the colour honest: these are optics and buyers care about true finish, so correct the cast, don't restyle the product. When you're done, tell me, per photo, exactly the white-balance and exposure move you landed on and the final pixel size, so I can trust the set is genuinely matched and every product prints sharp.

Second, the heroes: from each corrected shot, isolate the product off its messy seamless and set it on a pure #FFFFFF background per the marketplace hero spec — no gradient, no invented scene, nothing composited or painted onto the product — and deliver each as an exact 1:1 square at 1600 x 1600. The grey card and swatch must be gone from the delivered hero (keep me a copy of the corrected shot WITH the card still in it so we can both confirm the neutral). Because these come off real distributor cameras the files are large, so the square hero is a crop-and-downscale of the real frame — never blow a small crop up to fill the square.

Third, the distributor marks: two of my distributors want their brand mark on the line sheet, and both sent me raw scans of their marks — Harlow Optics Group's crest and Vantage Field Supply's nameplate. However you prep them, I need both to come out as clean, print-ready brand assets that drop cleanly into the card's mark window and stay razor-sharp at print size on every card.

Finally, build the line sheet: I've hand-built the InDesign product-card template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (product hero and distributor mark), and I'm giving you the SKU sheet. Merge them so every SKU gets its own card with its name, model code, finish and price bound in, its matched square hero dropped into the product window, and its distributor's mark in the mark window — then hand back a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF, one card per SKU. Bind the names, model codes and distributors verbatim from the sheet; don't invent or reassign anything. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point (checked on the card-bearing copies); every delivered hero an exact 1600 x 1600 pure-white square with the card cropped out and the product at print resolution in the card window; the two distributor marks each prepped the correct way and razor-sharp at print size; and exactly one finished card per SKU row.

inputs.name: sku01_thermal_monocular_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product photograph of a handheld thermal monocular (matte graphite cylindrical body, rubberized eyepiece, control buttons, short accessory rail) laid on an off-white / pale-grey seamless paper sweep in a small product studio. A standard 18% neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch sit flat on the sweep at the lower-left edge of the frame. Shot under COOL blue-white LED shop light with a distinct cyan cast and a slightly flat, marginally under-exposed exposure, loose uneven framing, soft contact shadow. Sharp real product detail — visible rubber texture, tiny scuffs on the matte finish, real plastic speculars — not glossy CGI. Rendered large, roughly 3200 x 3200 px, so there is headroom to crop the card out and still clear print resolution.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-01, cool/LED cast, flat/under-exposed. Correction sign: WARM + lift exposure. Matte graphite reads neutral so it is a WB restraint case (over-warming muddies it). Grey card in frame is the neutralisation target; rendered oversized so the square hero is a downscale, never an upscale. Distributor: Harlow (flat crest mark).

inputs.name: sku02_laser_rangefinder_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product photograph of a compact laser rangefinder monocular with a SATURATED blaze-orange polymer housing and black rubber armour, laid on a pale-grey seamless sweep. A standard 18% grey reference card and small white swatch sit at the lower-right edge of the frame. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with a strong orange cast and slightly bright exposure so the already-vivid orange housing is pushed near-glowing and starts to clip in the brightest facets. Real polymer texture, moulded seams, rubber grip detail, soft contact shadow. Un-graded distributor catalog shot, not CGI. Roughly 3400 x 3400 px.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-02, warm/tungsten cast, bright. Correction sign: COOL (opposite of SKU-01). UNDISCLOSED TRAP: the blaze-orange is a saturated finish already near clipping; neutralising the warm cast plus any reflexive 'make the product pop' vibrance/contrast lift drives it radioactive and blows the highlight facets. Correct move RESTRAINS highlights/whites/saturation while cooling the cast — the opposite reflex to the dull SKUs. Distributor: Vantage (anodized nameplate mark).

inputs.name: sku03_trail_camera_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product photograph of an olive-drab bark-camo trail camera (rugged rectangular plastic housing, lens and IR array on the front, latch on the side) laid on a pale-grey seamless sweep. A standard 18% grey card and small white swatch sit at the frame edge. Shot under GREENISH fluorescent work-light with a clear green tint AND noticeably under-exposed / dark. Real matte plastic and camo-print texture, latch and hinge detail, faint contact shadow. Un-graded distributor shot, not CGI. Roughly 3200 x 3200 px.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-03, green fluorescent cast + dark. Correction is TWO-AXIS: push tint toward magenta to kill the green while neutralising the card, plus a real exposure/shadow lift — not a single temperature slide. Olive-drab is close to the green cast, so an over-magenta or over-warm move visibly falsifies the housing colour. Distributor: Harlow (flat crest mark).

inputs.name: sku04_spotting_scope_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product photograph of a matte-black angled spotting scope body (large objective bell, focus ring, short built-in sunshade) laid on a pale-grey seamless sweep. A standard 18% grey card and small white swatch sit at the frame edge. Shot under OVEREXPOSED near-daylight so the top of the objective bell and the focus ring have hot, near-blown speculars. Real matte-black finish with fine texture, rubber focus-ring ribbing, soft contact shadow. Un-graded distributor shot, not CGI. Roughly 3600 x 3600 px.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-04, overexposed near-daylight. Tonal recovery DOMINATES: pull exposure/highlights/whites down to recover the blown speculars first, then a small WB nudge so the grey card lands neutral on the shared white point. Matte black is a black-point discipline case — don't crush it filling in the recovery. Distributor: Vantage (anodized nameplate mark).

inputs.name: sku05_tripod_head_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product photograph of a silver machined-aluminium ball-head tripod mount (anodised bright metal, knurled locking knobs, quick-release plate) laid on a pale-grey seamless sweep. A standard 18% grey card and small white swatch sit at the frame edge. Shot under near-neutral but FLAT, low-contrast light, slightly dull. Real brushed-metal micro-texture, knurling, subtle speculars, faint contact shadow. Un-graded distributor shot, not CGI. Roughly 3300 x 3300 px.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-05, near-neutral but flat. The grey card is already close to neutral so only a SMALL WB nudge is right — over-correcting pushes this off the set and tints the bright metal. The real work is tonal (add contrast/clarity to match the set feel) without clipping the metal speculars. Restraint case. Distributor: Harlow (flat crest mark).

inputs.name: sku06_night_vision_goggle_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product photograph of a monocular night-vision goggle (matte-black housing, a single round objective lens with a green-tinted anti-reflective coating, head-mount arm) laid on a pale-grey seamless sweep. A standard 18% grey card and small white swatch sit at the frame edge. Shot under STRONG cool blue window-shade light AND dark / under-exposed so the black housing muddies toward the shadows. Real matte housing texture and a believable green lens sheen, soft contact shadow. Un-graded distributor shot, not CGI. Roughly 3400 x 3400 px.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-06, strong blue cast + dark — the BIGGEST correction in the set: warm strongly and lift shadows/exposure while neutralising the card, proof that one batch number cannot serve every frame. Protect the green anti-reflective lens sheen (a real product feature) from being neutralised away as if it were a cast. Distributor: Vantage (anodized nameplate mark).

inputs.name: sku07_red_dot_sight_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product photograph of a compact gunmetal-grey red-dot reflex optic (open-frame housing, glass window, adjustment turrets, low mount) laid on a pale-grey seamless sweep. A standard 18% grey card and small white swatch sit at the frame edge. Shot under MIXED warm-key / cool-fill light, only mildly off overall. Real anodised metal micro-texture, turret knurling, glass reflection, soft contact shadow. Un-graded distributor shot, not CGI. Roughly 3200 x 3200 px.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-07, mixed and only mildly off — a modest, careful correction to bring the card neutral on the shared white point without overshooting. Gunmetal near-neutral, so restraint again. Distributor: Harlow (flat crest mark).

inputs.name: sku08_chronograph_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal product photograph of a coyote-tan ballistic chronograph unit (rectangular sensor body with a small display, folding sunshade rails, tripod socket) laid on a pale-grey seamless sweep. A standard 18% grey card and small white swatch sit at the frame edge. Shot under WARM tungsten light and DULL / low-contrast. Real matte polymer texture, display bezel, screw detail, soft contact shadow. Un-graded distributor shot, not CGI. Roughly 3300 x 3300 px.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU-08, warm + dull. Cool a touch to neutralise the card and add vibrance/clarity to match the set — but coyote-tan is a near-neutral warm fabric-like finish, so over-cooling greys it and over-vibrance turns it orange. Restraint case superficially resembling the warm-cast SKUs but its correct answer is small. Distributor: Vantage (anodized nameplate mark).

inputs.name: harlow_crest_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A raw raster scan (flatbed-style PNG) of a printed two-colour crest logo for a fictional optics distributor 'Harlow Optics Group': a simple geometric reticle-and-summit emblem with a short clean wordmark beneath, printed in solid dark-charcoal ink on off-white paper — flat solid colour, no gradients, no sheen, no photographic texture, hard printed edges, sitting slightly off-centre on the scanned paper with a thin uneven margin. Small raster PNG roughly 900 x 900 px, exactly as a distributor would scan and email it.
inputs.realism_notes: SOLUTION-SIDE (not shown to the agent): flat, high-contrast, solid-fill printed line art — the mark that CAN honestly become a clean SVG after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds + crisp + image_vectorize). One of the two triage inputs; supplied as a raw raster *_scan.png exactly like the Vantage mark, with a neutral name, so nothing in the input's kind or filename reveals which treatment it needs — the agent must decide by looking. gemini-3-pro-image chosen because it carries legible type at crisp edges. Produced output the agent registers for the merge: the vector mark 'harlow_mark'.

inputs.name: vantage_nameplate_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A raw raster scan (PNG) of a printed anodised-aluminium distributor nameplate reading 'VANTAGE FIELD SUPPLY', captured on a dark surface: a brushed-metal plate with engraved lettering, a bright anodised finish, specular highlights, subtle radial brush texture and soft reflections across the metal. A genuine metal object with real sheen and tonal gradients, not flat printed line art. Roughly 1600 x 1000 px, exactly as a distributor would scan/photograph and email it.
inputs.realism_notes: SOLUTION-SIDE (not shown to the agent): THE TRIAGE / TRAP asset. It is supplied as the SAME kind of raw raster *_scan.png as the Harlow crest, with a neutral name — nothing in the input's kind, filename or the CSV reveals its treatment, so the agent must recognise by looking that it is a photographed brushed-metal surface full of speculars and gradients. Feeding it to image_vectorize returns a flat, muddy silhouette that destroys the metal. Correct treatment is crop-to-bounds -> image_remove_background to transparency -> keep as a high-resolution raster placed via @dist_mark. Getting it wrong is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the Vantage cards print flat and dead. Produced output the agent registers for the merge: the raster mark 'vantage_mark'.

inputs.name: cragmoor_product_card.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD product line-sheet card (~100 x 150 mm portrait with 3 mm bleed) — ONE SKU per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<sku_name>>, <<model_code>>, <<finish>>, <<price>>, <<distributor>>, AND TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a square 1:1 product-hero window bound to @hero, and a small rectangular distributor-mark window bound to @dist_mark. The <<sku_name>> text frame has Auto-Size 'shrink to fit' enabled so long product names bind without going overset. The Cragmoor masthead, the column rules and the spec-label furniture are already drawn into the template artwork (fixed on every card), so the only per-row imagery is the hero and the distributor mark. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output: a converted-PDF template has no live merge fields and no data-merge image field, so it would not bind.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record per-SKU card is the correct, connector-doable shape (not a multi-up sheet, which the tool cannot place). Two image columns (@hero, @dist_mark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. Column names must exactly match the SKU-sheet headers.

inputs.name: cragmoor_sku_sheet.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: sku_name,model_code,finish,price,distributor,@hero,@dist_mark and 8 rows (one per SKU, in SKU-01..SKU-08 order). sku_name is a descriptive fictional product name including at least two DELIBERATELY LONG names (e.g. 'Cragmoor Ridgeline 640 Handheld Thermal Monocular', 35+ chars) alongside short ones so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. model_code is a short fictional code (e.g. CM-TM640). finish is the honest finish colour (Graphite, Blaze Orange, Olive Drab, Matte Black, Silver, Matte Black/Green, Gunmetal, Coyote Tan). price is a plausible USD price string. distributor is exactly 'Harlow Optics Group' for SKU-01/03/05/07 and 'Vantage Field Supply' for SKU-02/04/06/08. @hero holds hero_sku01.jpg ... hero_sku08.jpg in row order (the produced square marketplace heroes the agent registers under those exact names). @dist_mark points each row at its distributor's produced brand-mark asset by a neutral registered name — Harlow rows -> harlow_mark, Vantage rows -> vantage_mark — WITHOUT any file extension or type token, so the sheet never encodes whether a mark is vector or raster; the agent triages each raw mark scan itself and registers its produced output under that exact name for the merge to bind. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields and the two @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight cards (page-count = row-count gate). The @hero / @dist_mark columns hold the neutral names the agent must produce and register its outputs under, so naming discipline is a real dependency. CRITICAL DE-LEAK: @dist_mark carries only distributor-keyed neutral names (harlow_mark / vantage_mark) with NO extension and NO type column, so no client-supplied field telegraphs which mark is vector and which is raster — the agent must decide by looking at the two raw *_scan.png marks. SOLUTION-SIDE only (never in the sheet): the Harlow rows should resolve to the agent's VECTOR crest and the Vantage rows to the agent's TRANSPARENT-GROUND RASTER nameplate, proving both image columns and the triage both land in the deliverable. Long names exercise the auto-fit frame. Text-only merge (document_merge_data_vector) is the WRONG tool here — it cannot bind the two image columns.

outputs.name: heroes_matched_x8
outputs.spec: Eight pure-white marketplace hero images (hero_sku01.jpg .. hero_sku08.jpg), each: neutralised to its in-frame 18% grey card and matched to ONE shared white point and brightness across the whole batch while staying true to the real finish (no product recoloured, no strong finish colour clipped); the product isolated off its seamless and set on a solid pure #FFFFFF background (no gradient, no invented scene, nothing composited onto the product); the grey card and white swatch cropped OUT; delivered as an exact 1:1 square at 1600 x 1600 px, sRGB JPEG, downscaled from the camera-scale source (never enlarged). Card exclusion is graded on these delivered heroes; neutrality is graded on the retained card-bearing masters below. Acceptance (grader-checked): every delivered hero exactly 1600 x 1600, pure-white ground, card absent; the batch reads as one white point; each hero >= 300 DPI in the card's hero window. The agent must REPORT its final per-SKU white-balance (temp/tint) and exposure move AND the final pixel size. DELIVERABLE 1.

outputs.name: corrected_masters_cardin_x8
outputs.spec: Eight RETAINED corrected masters (master_sku01 .. master_sku08), the neutralised full frame of each SKU with the 18% grey card and white swatch STILL in frame (before knockout/crop). These are the artifacts the grader measures neutrality on. Acceptance (grader-checked): on every master the grey card reads visually neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance of each other) and the set shares one white point/brightness; no white swatch clipped to 255, no shadow crushed to 0. Retained deliverable so neutrality is checkable on the reference region even though the heroes crop the card out. DELIVERABLE 2.

outputs.name: distributor_marks_prepped
outputs.spec: The two distributor marks prepped triage-correct from their raw *_scan.png inputs and registered under the neutral names the SKU sheet references: 'harlow_mark' as clean vector line art traced only AFTER crop-to-bounds + crisp prep (razor edges at any card size), and 'vantage_mark' as the photographed anodised nameplate cropped and knocked to transparency then kept as a high-resolution raster (>= 300 px on the long edge so it prints >= 300 DPI in the mark window) — deliberately NOT vectorized, so the brushed-metal sheen survives to print. The correct vector-vs-raster split is the agent's own triage decision (nothing in the brief, the input names or the CSV tells it which is which). DELIVERABLE 3.

outputs.name: cragmoor_linesheet_x8_pdf
outputs.spec: Eight per-SKU product line-sheet cards, ONE PDF card per CSV row (page-count = row-count = 8), produced by merging cragmoor_sku_sheet.csv into the authored cragmoor_product_card.indd via document_merge_data_layout and exported with document_render_layout to a press-ready ~300 DPI 100 x 150 mm + 3 mm bleed PDF: each card binds <<sku_name>>/<<model_code>>/<<finish>>/<<price>>/<<distributor>> verbatim from the row, drops that SKU's matched square hero into the @hero window and the correct distributor mark into the @dist_mark window (vector crest for Harlow rows, transparent-ground anodized raster for Vantage rows), and the auto-fit name frame absorbs the long names without clipping. Acceptance gate: card/page count == data row count == 8 (a broken or empty-frame merge fails this); each placed hero renders >= 300 DPI at the card trim. DELIVERABLE 4 — the owned composed endpoint.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: sku01_thermal_monocular_raw.jpg, sku02_laser_rangefinder_raw.jpg, sku03_trail_camera_raw.jpg, sku04_spotting_scope_raw.jpg, sku05_tripod_head_raw.jpg, sku06_night_vision_goggle_raw.jpg, sku07_red_dot_sight_raw.jpg, sku08_chronograph_raw.jpg, harlow_crest_scan.png, vantage_nameplate_scan.png, cragmoor_product_card.indd, cragmoor_sku_sheet.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the eight raw distributor product photos, the two distributor marks, the authored .indd product-card template and the SKU CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has a real asset reference. (Single upload — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.)

SKU-01 (cool LED, flat/under): WARM the temperature and nudge tint OFF cyan, and lift exposure/contrast slightly, until the in-frame 18% grey card reads truly neutral and the frame reaches the shared brightness target — but restrain the warming so the neutral graphite body does not turn muddy-warm. Per-image delta reasoned to THIS card, not a batch constant. Report the temp/tint/exposure landed on. This neutralised frame (card still in) is RETAINED as corrected master 1. Replaces the killed original's parameterless auto-ops and the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature.

Isolate the monocular onto a solid pure #FFFFFF ground via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}) — the CORRECT knockout path: it removes the seamless AND the grey card/white swatch and drops the product on marketplace-compliant white. Deliberately NOT image_select_subject -> image_invert_selection -> image_fill_area: select_subject is person-oriented and mis-fires on a bare product, and fill_area solids the whole masked region flat. No enclosed interior hole is claimed (outer-background isolation only).

Crop the white-ground isolate to a centred 1:1 square and downscale to EXACTLY 1600 x 1600, sRGB. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only — never canvas-extend, never enlarge past the ~3200 px source. The grey card is already gone (removed with the background), so the delivered hero is card-free. Feeds both the heroes deliverable and the @hero cell for SKU-01. Report final px (1600 x 1600).

SKU-02 (warm tungsten, bright, SATURATED blaze-orange): move the OPPOSITE way from SKU-01 — COOL the temperature until the grey card neutralises on the shared white point, and CRITICALLY pull highlights/whites DOWN and hold saturation so the already-hot orange housing stops clipping. Do NOT add vibrance/contrast to 'make it pop' — that blows the orange radioactive (the undisclosed trap). Restraint move. Report the settings. Retained as corrected master 2.
Isolate the rangefinder onto solid #FFFFFF via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); removes seamless + card + swatch. Same anti-pattern avoidance as step 3.
Centred 1:1 square, downscale to EXACTLY 1600 x 1600, sRGB. Downscale-only. Feeds SKU-02's @hero cell. Report final px.

SKU-03 (greenish fluorescent + dark): TWO-AXIS correction — push TINT toward magenta to kill the green while neutralising the card, PLUS a real exposure/shadow lift; a single temperature slide will not fix a green cast. Hold the correction so the olive-drab housing stays believably olive (over-magenta falsifies it). Report the move. Retained as corrected master 3.
Isolate the trail camera onto solid #FFFFFF via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); removes seamless + card + swatch.
Centred 1:1 square, downscale to EXACTLY 1600 x 1600, sRGB. Downscale-only. Feeds SKU-03's @hero cell. Report final px.

SKU-04 (overexposed near-daylight): TONAL RECOVERY dominates — pull exposure/highlights/whites DOWN to recover the blown speculars on the objective bell first, then a small WB nudge so the card lands neutral on the shared white point. Hold the black point so the matte-black body does not crush. Report the move. Retained as corrected master 4.
Isolate the spotting scope onto solid #FFFFFF via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); removes seamless + card + swatch. Matte-black-on-white edge cuts cleanly.
Centred 1:1 square, downscale to EXACTLY 1600 x 1600, sRGB. Downscale-only. Feeds SKU-04's @hero cell. Report final px.

SKU-05 (near-neutral, flat): the card is already close to neutral, so only a SMALL WB nudge is correct — over-correcting tints the bright anodised metal and pushes it off the set. Do the real work tonally: add contrast/clarity to match the set feel WITHOUT clipping the metal speculars. Restraint case. Report the (small WB, tonal) move. Retained as corrected master 5.

Isolate the tripod head onto solid #FFFFFF via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); removes seamless + card + swatch. Outer-background isolation only; any gap between the head arms is edge-connected, not an enclosed hole, so no enclosed-hole knockout is claimed.
Centred 1:1 square, downscale to EXACTLY 1600 x 1600, sRGB. Downscale-only. Feeds SKU-05's @hero cell. Report final px.

SKU-06 (strong blue cast + dark): the BIGGEST correction — warm STRONGLY and lift shadows/exposure to bring it up while neutralising the card to the shared white point; protect skin-of-the-product from muddying. Keep the green anti-reflective lens sheen (a real product feature) — do not neutralise it away as if it were a cast. Proof that one batch number cannot serve every frame. Report the move. Retained as corrected master 6.
Isolate the night-vision goggle onto solid #FFFFFF via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); removes seamless + card + swatch.
Centred 1:1 square, downscale to EXACTLY 1600 x 1600, sRGB. Downscale-only. Feeds SKU-06's @hero cell. Report final px.

SKU-07 (mixed warm-key/cool-fill, mildly off): a modest, careful correction to bring the card neutral on the shared white point without overshooting — gunmetal is near-neutral, so restraint again. Report the move. Retained as corrected master 7.
Isolate the red-dot sight onto solid #FFFFFF via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); removes seamless + card + swatch.
Centred 1:1 square, downscale to EXACTLY 1600 x 1600, sRGB. Downscale-only. Feeds SKU-07's @hero cell. Report final px.

SKU-08 (warm + dull): cool a touch to neutralise the card on the shared white point and add a little vibrance/clarity to match the set — but coyote-tan is near-neutral warm, so over-cooling greys it and over-vibrance turns it orange; keep it small. Report the move. With this the eight masters share one white point, each neutralised to its own card. Retained as corrected master 8.
Isolate the chronograph onto solid #FFFFFF via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); removes seamless + card + swatch.

Centred 1:1 square, downscale to EXACTLY 1600 x 1600, sRGB. Downscale-only. Feeds SKU-08's @hero cell. Steps 4/7/10/13/16/19/22/25 are the heroes_matched_x8 deliverable and the eight @hero cells the merge binds. Report final px.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into eight parallel per-SKU chains. Each SKU is a three-step chain: an adaptive image_apply_adjustments neutralisation whose correction SIGN and axis differ per frame (warm the cool LED SKU-01, cool+restrain the saturated warm SKU-02, magenta-tint+lift the green/dark SKU-03, tonally recover the overexposed SKU-04, small-WB+tone the flat SKU-05, strongly warm+lift the blue/dark SKU-06, modestly correct the mixed SKU-07, small-cool+vibrance the warm/dull SKU-08) — each neutralised frame RETAINED as a card-bearing corrected master — then image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}) to isolate the product on pure white (removing seamless + card + swatch), then image_crop_and_resize to an exact 1600 x 1600 square (downscale-only). The two distributor marks arrive as the SAME kind of raw raster *_scan.png (harlow_crest_scan.png, vantage_nameplate_scan.png) with neutral names, and the SKU sheet's @dist_mark carries only neutral registered names — so the agent must TRIAGE by looking, into two paths: the flat Harlow crest runs crop_to_bounds -> crisp adjustments -> image_vectorize into a clean SVG registered as 'harlow_mark' (26->27->28), while the photographed anodised Vantage nameplate diverges to crop_to_bounds -> image_remove_background(transparency) -> crop_and_resize into a high-res transparent raster registered as 'vantage_mark' (29->30->31), deliberately never touching image_vectorize. The eight square heroes plus the two prepped marks converge into document_merge_data_layout (32), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the SKU CSV and emits one merged card per row, resolving BOTH @hero and @dist_mark per row (the @dist_mark cells bind the agent's OWN produced marks by their neutral names); the merged set is exported to the per-SKU press PDF (33). Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; the merge converges all ten image chains plus the template and CSV. 33 calls, 8 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship rebuilt from the killed single-SKU / ten-auto-op version: 33 connector calls, 8 distinct Adobe tools, one batch upload fanning into eight dependent per-SKU chains plus a two-way triage that all converge on a genuine composed endpoint (an authored-.indd data merge). Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: the eight neutralisations are NOT one recipe run eight times — each is a per-image white-balance/exposure decision whose SIGN and dominant axis differ (cool frames warmed, warm frames cooled, a green frame fixed on tint plus an exposure lift, an overexposed frame tonally recovered, near-neutral frames held with restraint), all forced to converge on one measurable target (the in-frame 18% grey card), so the naive move of pushing one correction through all eight visibly fails the match; a saturated blaze-orange SKU adds an undisclosed clip trap that punishes a reflexive 'make it pop'. The knockout must use remove_background({backgroundColor}) — the tempting select_subject->invert->fill_area path both mis-fires (person-oriented selector on a bare product) and flat-solids the mask; every square hero is a downscale to an exact 1600 x 1600 from a camera-scale source, never an upscale. On top sits a genuine two-way triage of two superficially-similar distributor marks (flat crest vectorized after prep-before-trace; photographed anodised nameplate knocked to transparency and kept as raster because a trace would flatten the metal) whose wrong treatment is invisible until print, and a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template gated on page-count==row-count and >=300 DPI. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no compositing, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; image_fill_area and image_apply_color_overlay are unused; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature/_highlights/_vibrance_and_saturation/_brightness_and_contrast are replaced by image_apply_adjustments; no enclosed-interior-hole knockout is claimed.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): (1) each SKU carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance criterion is that every RETAINED card-bearing master reads a clean neutral with the whole set matched to one white point — a target the agent can miss by eye — with the agent required to REPORT the final per-SKU white-balance/exposure move and final pixel size, so an eyeballed or uniform correction is caught; (2) the two distributor marks arrive as the SAME kind of raw raster *_scan.png with neutral names, and the SKU sheet's @dist_mark carries only neutral registered names (harlow_mark / vantage_mark) with no extension or type token — so nothing client-supplied telegraphs the answer and the agent must TRIAGE by looking, prepping them by DIFFERENT correct paths (vectorize the flat crest; knock the photographed anodised nameplate to transparency and keep it raster, registering each produced output under the neutral name the merge binds), where vectorizing the metal scan yields a dead flat silhouette; (3) the knockout must be remove_background({backgroundColor}) — the select_subject->invert->fill_area path mis-fires and flat-fills; (4) the merged PDF page-count must equal the CSV row-count (8) with each hero placed >=300 DPI. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (a) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target across eight frames shot under opposite casts and exposures, each needing its own sign/axis of correction while holding near-neutral finishes (graphite, silver, gunmetal, coyote-tan) believable and protecting a real green-lens feature; (b) constraint-reasoning around tool limits — knockout via remove_background({backgroundColor}) not select->invert->fill, exact-square heroes by downscale-only crop_and_resize from camera-scale sources (never image_fill_area canvas-extension, the killed original's defect), image placement only via a genuine two-@-image-column .indd merge; (c) the two-way distributor-mark triage. TRAP THE BRIEF DOES NOT DISCLOSE: the brief calls the blaze-orange SKU only a 'finish', never warning it is a saturated colour already near clipping, so the reflexive post-neutralisation vibrance/contrast 'pop' blows it radioactive — the correct move restrains highlights/saturation, the opposite reflex to the dull SKUs; a second undisclosed trap is that one of the two 'distributor marks' is a photographed metal object that cannot survive a trace. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side): every grey card neutral on its retained master and the set on one white point, per-SKU WB/exposure + final px reported; every delivered hero exactly 1600 x 1600 pure-white with the card cropped out and >=300 DPI in the card window; the two marks prepped triage-correct (clean vector + transparent-ground raster >=300 px); exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI 100 x 150 mm card per SKU row.
